title: Urban Agglomerations Environmental Heterogeneity and Heatwave Risks: Spatiotemporal Insights from Remote Sensing and Public Sentiment Analysis
content: Climate change has intensified urban heatwaves, creating significant public health challenges. Despite their importance, the causality linking environmental factors to heatwave dynamics, and heatwaves to public sentiment across urban agglomerations remain poorly understood. Here we apply established analytical methods to investigate these relationships across five major Chinese urban agglomerations (2014-2023). Using Generalized Convergent Cross Mapping (GCCM), we identify asymmetric causality between environmental variables and heatwave characteristics, with surface albedo showing the strongest causality (mean ρ=0.772) on heatwave intensity indicators, particularly in northern urban agglomerations. Vegetation cover and thermal indices also played significant but regionally variable roles. Bayesian Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) revealed marked spatial heterogeneity, with Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Yangtze River Delta exhibiting the highest positive random effects. Social media sentiment analysis identified five distinct regional response patterns to heatwaves. Sentiment shows a nonlinear response to heatwaves. Heat perception and thermal discomfort rise steadily. Health concern and outdoor activity reduction show a threshold effect at moderate intensity. Energy consumption concerns rise sharply only at high intensity, and regional differences are significant. These findings clarify the spatially heterogeneous drivers of urban heatwaves and reveal nonlinear, region-specific public emotional responses, providing a scientific basis for targeted climate adaptation and public health strategies.
